items.title: S&P 500 profit margins spiked to 16.7% in Q2, which is by far their highest level in history. “Profit margins are probably the most mean-reverting series in finance, and if profit margins don't mean revert, then something has gone badly wrong with capitalism. If high profits don't attract competition, there's something wrong with the system.”
items.content:
S&P 500 profit margins spiked to 16.7% in Q2, which is by far their highest level in history.

“Profit margins are probably the most mean-reverting series in finance, and if profit margins don't mean revert, then something has gone badly wrong with capitalism. If high profits don't attract competition, there's something wrong with the system.” - Jeremy Grantham
— Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello) Aug 3, 2026

items.title: S&P 500 Q2 earnings are on pace to rise 47% YoY, the highest growth rate since Q2 2021. We've never seen earnings growth this high outside of post-recessionary rebounds. This is an unprecedented boom fueled by massive EPS gains in big tech, including markups in SpaceX/Anthropic.

items.title: Amazon revenues increased 20% YoY to a new Q2 record of $201 billion. Net Income increased 245% YoY to $63 billion, the highest quarterly profit in company history ($42 billion from unrealized gains). Operating margins increased to a record 13.7% from 11.4% a year ago. $AMZN
